- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.25), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is high (0.75–1.00) and model forecasts are rising, check for mean reversion; if price has been trending up for 5+ days, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.25–0.67), model often underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for potential downside.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–3 day lag in true price drop.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model is prone to persistent underestimation; apply a 1–2% upward bias to counteract mean reversion bias.
